headline: GOLD CLINGS TO $4,300 SUPPORT: August CPI Day Puts Fed Hike Odds at 70%, Third Weekly Loss at Risk
snippet: Gold tested the critical $4,300 support zone Friday as traders braced for the August CPI report — the last major inflation data before the September 15-16 Fed meeting. Spot gold is on track for its third straight weekly decline after Thursday's PPI printed at 5.4% annually, lifting rate-hike odds to 70%; a hot headline CPI could push gold toward $4,100, while a cooler-than-expected core reading may trigger a recovery toward the $4,400 area.

headline: SILVER TURNS NEGATIVE: At $64 on CPI Day, Industrial Demand Meets Fed Hike Headwind
snippet: Silver futures turned negative Friday at $64 per ounce heading into the August CPI release, extending a weekly loss driven by elevated Fed rate-hike expectations after Thursday's 5.4% PPI. Silver is uniquely squeezed: investment demand retreats on rate-hike fears while structural industrial buying from solar manufacturers persists — leaving the metal exposed to outsized drawdown when the rate-hike narrative dominates, despite the ongoing physical market deficit.

headline: HOW TO READ TODAY'S CPI WITHOUT FLINCHING: Gold's Bull Case Survives a Hot Print
snippet: Advantage Gold argues investors conditioned to fear a hot CPI print are misreading the current gold market: the real question isn't whether inflation ticks higher this month, but whether the Fed can actually return it to 2% without breaking growth — and bond market reluctance to fully price in that outcome leaves gold's structural bull case intact regardless of today's number. The piece provides a practical framework for separating short-term rate-hike noise from the long-term debasement bid that carried gold from $2,000 to $4,350.

headline: WORLD'S BIGGEST COPPER FIND GROWS 30%: Ivanhoe's Makoko Hits 12 Million Tonnes Contained Copper
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines expanded its Makoko District at the Western Forelands project in the DRC by 30%, updating indicated resources to 42 million tonnes at 2.66% copper and inferred resources to 612 million tonnes at 1.80% copper — approximately 12 million tonnes of contained copper in the world's largest and highest-grade copper discovery of the past decade. About 60,000 metres of 2026 drilling was not yet incorporated, and mineralization remains open in multiple directions, suggesting the resource is far from mature.

headline: RIO TINTO MOVES ON CAPE YORK: Acquires Aurukun Bauxite From Glencore and Mitsubishi Ahead of Gove Closure
snippet: Rio Tinto agreed to acquire the Aurukun bauxite project in Queensland's Cape York Peninsula from Glencore and Mitsubishi Development for undisclosed terms, consolidating its position in a region where it already mines over 30 million tonnes of bauxite annually. The deal comes as Rio prepares to wind down its Gove bauxite mine in the Northern Territory by 2030, making Aurukun — still subject to permitting and community approvals — a strategically critical long-term feed source.

headline: UK COPPER MINER BUYS INTO QUEBEC: CAML's A$232M All-Share Cygnus Deal Adds High-Grade Chibougamau
snippet: London-listed Central Asia Metals (LSE: CAML) agreed to acquire Cygnus Metals through an all-share scheme of arrangement valuing the Australian explorer at approximately A$232 million, gaining 100% of the Chibougamau Copper-Gold Project in Quebec — 6.4 million tonnes at 2.3% copper and 0.8 g/t gold in measured and indicated resources. Cygnus shareholders vote on the scheme this month, with CAML retaining roughly 70% of the enlarged company and adding Canadian copper development exposure alongside its producing Macedonia and Kazakhstan assets.

headline: QUEENSLAND COKING COAL CONSOLIDATES: Stanmore Adds 724 Million Tonnes via $105M Moranbah South Deal
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) agreed to acquire 100% of Exxaro Resources' Moranbah South tenements in Queensland for US$105 million, adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated premium hard coking coal resources directly adjacent to its Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects. The deal, expected to close before year-end 2026 pending FIRB and ACCC approval, also cancels significant prior payment obligations tied to Isaac Downs Extension, materially improving project economics.

headline: TIMMINS CAMP WIDENS: New Break Drills 3.46 g/t Au Over 38.6m and Finds Gold in New Syenite Rock Type
snippet: New Break Resources (TSXV: NBR) drilled 3.46 g/t gold over 38.6 metres at its Moray Gold Project 49 km southeast of Timmins, Ontario, while also intercepting gold in syenite for the first time — opening a potential new style of mineralization beyond the previously known volcanic host rocks. With 5,372 metres drilled in 32 holes in 2026 and four holes still pending assay, the syenite discovery could significantly expand the total target footprint.

headline: NORTHWEST ONTARIO: Gold X2 Mining Hits 173m at 0.89 g/t Au Beneath Existing Pit at Moss Project
snippet: Gold X2 Mining Inc. (TSXV: AUXX) reported 173.0 metres at 0.89 g/t gold from its QES Zone resource expansion program at the Moss Gold Project in Northwest Ontario, intersected 100 metres beneath the existing RPEEE pit. The result is from a 21-hole program targeting depth extensions of a bulk-tonnage mineralized system; 12 holes have been completed and the intercept demonstrates strong grade continuity well below the current resource shell.

headline: TASMANIA COPPER FOOTPRINT GROWS: G11 Resources Designs Three New Holes as Zig Zag Alteration Zone Hits 90m
snippet: G11 Resources (ASX: G11) is redesigning its drill program at the Zig Zag copper-gold target in Tasmania after hole SD2602 intercepted approximately 90 metres of silica-sericite-pyrite alteration with elevated silver, arsenic and antimony — a textbook porphyry indicator — adjacent to Sibanye-Stillwater's Mt Lyell copper-gold mine, which recently approved its restart with first ore targeted for 2029. Three new angled holes are planned to test the northern extension of the alteration zone, with assays pending.
